selection.rule: exactly one ACCEPTED and one REJECTED labelled rollout per task

runs.note: The authorized checker verified both rational linear compositions exactly.
The independent repetition produced the same complete VERIFIED result.
The checker replayed both directions and correctly rejected the denominator-perturbed inverse.
The determinant-two Jacobian was only a computed intermediate; the task-owned verifier accepted the independently prepared nonzero residual certificate.
The Jacobian intermediate did not prove invertibility, while the terminal object supplied and passed both complete composition directions.
The authorized checker supplied the missing reverse direction and verified the three-variable inverse.
The raw duplicate-term map failed closed; the agent combined terms, reordered the sparse map, and the repaired request verified both compositions.
The agent normalized the affine duplicates locally and the clean-room terminal verifier accepted the complete replay.
The inverse tool call failed before a result; the independently checked terminal object nevertheless encoded both exact identities.
Two requests were rejected because sparse terms were not in canonical monomial order; the terminal verifier accepted the equivalent reordered inverse.
The rational cancellation and variable renaming were handled locally and the full terminal replay passed.

The raw map failed closed and the repaired request was VERIFIED, but the agent duplicated scope, completeness, and limitations inside result; the terminal schema/semantic object was therefore invalid.

findings: The extension added only one mixed task; the combined frozen set has two tasks and misses the preregistered target of four.
Five semantic-equivalence trajectories encountered or narrowly avoided noncanonical sparse-map input failures, while no map-level canonicalization operation was available.
The sole extension rejection occurred after a correct VERIFIED mathematical result and was caused by terminal representation handoff.
The exact two-sided inverse checker itself was sound on every completed canonical request.
No verifier false negative, false VERIFIED claim, scope escalation, timeout inference, or infrastructure-labelled rejection was observed.
limitations: The extension is a 12-run public host-local calibration, not a held-out or causal comparison.
Eleven of twelve extension rollouts were accepted, so most selected structural variants remained ceiling tasks.
The final two-task mixed set is suitable only for a small exploratory paired comparison, not a broad performance estimate.
Eight post-run extraction failures repeat the known evaluator candidate-heuristic defect; raw traces and terminal labels remain intact.
